matches.rationale: No finding identifies the inconsistency between the tabulated SE/SE_peak metrics in Figure 6(b) and the learning curves in Figure 6(a).
Pred 1 detects a sign error in f^{return} that reverses the behavioral interpretation, matching the sign inconsistency and the mismatch between definition and stated goal.

Pred 8 describes the selective per-environment tuning of p and reporting only the best, without disclosing the chosen values, which directly matches the ground-truth criticism of undisclosed hyperparameter selection.

Pred 9 identifies that the abstract claims 'completely eliminates sample inefficiency' etc. while the evidence only shows partial improvement, aligning with the overstatement described in the ground truth.
No finding mentions the possibly fabricated or premature citations Cheng et al. 2025 or Deng et al. 2025.
No finding discusses the omission of ethical considerations and safety discussion for RLHF toxicity mitigation.
Pred 9 also flags the exaggerated marketing language in the introduction ('unprecedented', 'solves ... instability'), capturing the rhetorical exaggeration targeted by this ground truth.

Pred 4 highlights the contradiction between a fixed pre-trained reference policy and a dynamic reference that evolves with training, corresponding exactly to the inconsistent reference-policy description between Section 3.1 and Appendix A.2.
Pred 10 reports that Figure 6's y-axis ranges are optimized to highlight superiority and that early rounds are omitted, matching the ground-truth description of visual encoding manipulation.
Pred 8 notes that the best p is selected separately per environment without a tuning budget for baselines, which is the same unfair experimental design identified in the ground truth.

Pred 14 points out that the claim of statistically significant improvement is overbroad and that confidence intervals are missing for several environments, aligning with the ground truth's concern about inconsistent improvement and high variance.
Pred 3 captures the notational inconsistency in the influence score formula—using theta_0^{(k)} versus theta_j^{(k)}—which matches the ground-truth ambiguity about which checkpoint is used.
No finding addresses the non-reporting of additional environments or negative results beyond the six benchmark environments.

Pred 13 identifies that the f^{return} objective is not the standard REINFORCE objective and that the citation to Sutton & Barto is misattributed, agreeing with the ground-truth claim of misattribution.
No finding points out the inconsistency between the claimed negligible overhead and the substantial influence-calculation times reported in Appendices B.9 and Table 6.
